items.title: Fusion and rerank cut loss: ranked gold discarded when legs are fused into a small pool
items.problem: Gold turns that one retrieval leg ranks well are dropped when the legs are fused into a small candidate pool (especially lexical-only or vector-only evidence that no other leg corroborates), and some survivors are dropped by a fixed keep-line while the token budget is half empty.
items.gap: B7/B9/B10/I75/I78 are confirmed: protection stops at rank 3 per leg, fusion is rank-based, no fusion cut is logged. R14 contributes the rank-band table (best leg rank vs survival) that sizes a deeper protection value offline, and the convex-combination-versus-RRF question.
items.hypothesis: Protecting the top 8 per leg, fusing with score-normalised weights and letting the keep-line fill the token budget (about 15 anchors) keeps most of the 15 top-10 cuts and part of the 11-30 band, recovering 8-20 of 72 questions at zero model cost. Ceiling if every gold within depth 30 is kept: 20 questions.
items.evidence: 68 stage-b/cf fusion-cut questions plus 4 rerank-keep cuts; 11 of 15 top-10 cuts never entered the 20-pool; in-context rate 95.8% at best leg rank 4-10 falls to 67.9% at 21-30; 105 of 115 retrieval failures use under 3,000 of 4,096 tokens; 84 gold turns cut at fusion, 11 at rerank
items.method: measured (RET-4, RET-7, POS-2) from logged leg ranks to depth 60

solutions.name: Deeper per-leg protection
solutions.mechanism: Raise pool_protect_per_leg from 3 to 8 so BM25-top-10 or vector-top-10 gold survives fusion.

solutions.name: Score-aware fusion
solutions.mechanism: Convex combination of normalised scores instead of RRF k=60, calibrated on logged ranks.
solutions.risk: weights overfit to the dev conversations

solutions.name: Budget-driven keep
solutions.mechanism: Keep anchors until the token budget is filled (keep 15 or budget-driven) instead of a fixed 10.

solutions.name: Wider rerank pool
solutions.mechanism: Rerank 30-40 candidates, already queued as S67.

items.title: Explicit-date questions: the date is treated as ordinary words, no session-date prior at fusion
items.problem: A question that contains an explicit calendar date points at the session of that date, yet the engine treats the date as ordinary words; the gold turn is found by one leg and lost in fusion. The temporal leg fires on few questions and is off in the reference.
items.gap: B4/I8 sharpened: the loss is concentrated in explicit-date questions, not relative ones. Engine survey adds window overlap plus proximity boost inside the window instead of a hard span filter (Hindsight) and reference_time on every read (R14-time-2).

items.title: Multi-evidence recall: fixed depth, no coverage objective, weak aggregation trigger
items.problem: Questions that need three or more independent evidence items (list, count, 'all', 'both') get a fixed top-k anchor set. The chance that every needed item reaches the reader falls steeply with the number of items, and the trigger that deepens retrieval for such questions fires on fewer than half of them.
items.gap: B1 (aggregation retrieval) and I4 (list-mode trigger is an English regex): R14 adds the measured n_gold curve and the 37 missed-trigger questions. The 0-call trigger and the coverage objective are not built.
items.hypothesis: A trigger that combines question shape with the leg score profile fires on at least 70% of n_gold>=3 questions at no more than 15% false fire on single-gold ones; list-mode depth plus entity/session-diverse selection lifts all-gold-in-context for n_gold>=3 from 34% (non-list) to 50% or more, recovering 10-20 of 55 questions (about 0.6-1.3 points) without the cost of the slot loop.
items.evidence: 55 aggregation retrieval losses (39 exclusive primary pattern); 37 of them not in list mode; all-gold-in-context 95.9% at one gold turn falls to 8.7% as n_gold grows; list mode fires on 39% of n_gold>=3 questions
items.method: measured (RET-1, RET-11) on the reference full run; trigger precision/recall is a CPU computation over the 1,540 rows

solutions.name: Score-profile aggregation trigger
solutions.mechanism: Decide list-depth from question shape AND the retrieval score profile (flat top scores, many same-entity hits); no model call.
solutions.risk: false fire on single-gold questions adds distractors

solutions.name: Coverage-aware selection
solutions.mechanism: MMR-style selection with entity/session diversity so near-duplicates stop crowding the anchors.
solutions.risk: diversity can drop a true duplicate gold turn

solutions.name: Missing-slot second retrieval
solutions.mechanism: One bounded sufficiency check that names the missing slot, then exactly one targeted re-search (not the open slot loop).
solutions.source: IRCoT / Self-Ask [Trivedi2023-ircot] [Press2023-self-ask]; Mnemon ALL-need paging (R14-qry-2); EverOS sufficiency check (R14-hop-1)
solutions.risk: slot loop already measured net -3 at 8x cost; keep the bound

items.title: Over-refusal and premise denial: no typed commit route for judgement questions
items.problem: The reader answers 'not mentioned' or denies the premise when the evidence supports a committed inference (hypothetical, 'likely', world-knowledge hop). Prompt-only yes/no rules misfire on other question shapes, and abstention policy has no shared test.

items.title: Wrong detail and distractor use; one window size for every question shape
items.problem: The reader answers from a plausible sibling line: topical, near the gold line, but a different or generic detail. The distractor is a window neighbour of the gold in about a third of cases and a retrieval hit in over half. Context size is the same for every shape, so the window that helps temporal questions is paid for by single-hop distractors. Position effects (lost in the middle) do not reproduce at this context length.
items.gap: C1/C9/R2-4/I6 confirmed: reordering was rejected, verification not screened, owner/event check not built. R14 adds the negative position result (do not spend a screen), the per-shape window, and Mastra/MemOS style attached source context.
items.hypothesis: A binding check that the cited line shares the question's event noun phrase and date (code), plus one repair call on mismatches, removes about a third of true distractor cases (+10 to +14 questions); a per-shape window (1/1 for non-temporal single-hop) recovers about 1 point on single-hop at no loss on temporal.
items.evidence: 46 wrong_detail rows, 59 distractor-source rows (19 window neighbours, 32 retrieval hits); accuracy given all gold falls 91% (<=40 turns) to 83.6% (>60 turns); position quintiles 0.89-0.92 (Fisher p=0.90) so no position effect; rank>3 gold 74.8% vs 90.8%
items.method: measured/heuristic (READ-2, DIST-1, LEN-1, POS-1, POS-2); 13 hand-confirmed

solutions.name: Provenance check (owner/event/date binding)
solutions.mechanism: Code checks the cited line against the question's head noun phrase and date; one repair call on mismatch only.

solutions.name: Quote-then-answer
solutions.mechanism: Reader quotes the line first; the quote must contain the head noun phrase.

solutions.name: Per-shape window and budget
solutions.mechanism: Narrow window for single-fact shapes, wide for temporal and multi-turn.

solutions.name: Evidence compression
solutions.mechanism: Compress distractor-heavy context before reading.

items.title: Cross-session spread: turn-level, session-agnostic retrieval; summaries and episodes as legs
items.problem: Evidence for one question is spread over several sessions while retrieval is turn-level and session-agnostic; nothing asks whether each session that mentions the entity or topic is represented. Higher-grain units (session summary, episode, dated observation log) are the usual remedy, but the unit returned to the reader matters more than the quality of the summary text.
items.gap: B8 (sessions with no hit). R14 sharpens it to a per-session coverage objective and adds three engine ideas: render the parent summary next to each fact (MemOS background, Memori), return the parent unit with facts as keys (EverOS, Supermemory), and a dated always-in-context observation log without retrieval (Mastra OM).
items.hypothesis: A session-level leg followed by one best turn per matched session lifts all-gold coverage for n_sessions>=3 from 26% to 45% or more; rendering the parent summary line next to a hit adds context for 'which event' questions at under 200 tokens.
items.evidence: 43 questions with gold in three or more sessions; all-gold rate 35.8% at 3 sessions and 15.5% at 4+; in-context accuracy 72.9% at two sessions, 62.5% at three

items.title: Elliptical and context-dependent turns: decontextualisation and an index view
items.problem: Gold turns that are elliptical or anaphoric (a reply that carries the answer but not the topic) are unfindable because the topic lives in the neighbouring turn; a +-2 window around anchors reaches them only if the topical neighbour was itself found. items.title: Lexical-zero and paraphrase gold: surface form is the strongest predictor of a miss
items.problem: Gold turns that share almost no content words with the question (paraphrase, synonym, category-versus-instance wording) are missed by both lexical and dense legs. Neither the stored record nor the query is enriched with the vocabulary of the other.
items.gap: B2/B5/B6/B15 confirmed. R14 adds the engine finding that most engines expand at write time (keys per fact), not at query time, and the literature view that query-time HyDE is net-neutral when a strong hybrid plus reranker is in place.

items.evidence: 81 questions with gold turns of near-zero word overlap; word overlap is the strongest single predictor of a gold turn being found (embedding correlation about -0.48); 72 combined retrieval-stage questions are zero-overlap or BM25-miss with a vector hit

items.title: Indirect gold for judgement questions: evidence describes behaviour, never the question's words
items.problem: Open-domain (hypothetical or trait) questions ask for a judgement while the supporting turns describe behaviour; single-shot retrieval on the question text finds neither. The reader ceiling given all gold is also low.
items.gap: B3 confirmed; the class open_domain_inference_retrieval has no built primary solution in the solution map. OBS-06 proposes inference probes (S74).
items.hypothesis: Rewriting the question into 3-4 evidence-kind sub-queries (what X chose, enjoys, said about A, B) recovers about half the missing gold (14 of 28), but the 47% reader ceiling caps the accuracy gain at 4-7 questions.
items.evidence: 28 open-domain retrieval losses with 47.6% of their gold turns missing; reader accuracy given all gold 46.9% on cat3 (96 questions); 41 open-domain wrong answers are not refusals

items.title: Profile and attribute state with history; knowledge update; destructive edits
items.problem: User facts change over time. The store must track attribute values with history, supersede by event time, answer 'what is X's ...' from the keyed value rather than the first-ranked raw turn, and never destroy the old value. The profile card is built but no read path consumes it.
items.gap: G-W4 (extractor does not see keys of earlier facts) confirmed. OBS-04 proposes offline.person_attributes_v2 (S71). R14 adds: known-keys context to the extractor (Mnemon), predict-calibrate delta extraction (Nemori), a supersede-not-delete invariant (MemMachine/MIRIX defect), a judge-empty counter (Graphiti #1666) and read-time withdrawal of covered records.
items.hypothesis: Event-time-ordered supersede with the cardinality registry yields a correct current value and a history block; known-keys context removes duplicate-key facts and lets same-key supersession be model-driven; validate the history half on a knowledge-update benchmark.
items.evidence: 33 attribute questions (single-hop or multi-hop) wrong; profile_card_v2 has no read consumer (S46 skipped); standing answers and histories unscreened on a keyed-state arm

items.title: Entity aliasing and link tables: seed-to-neighbour expansion without per-session LLM graph builds
items.problem: Names appear as nicknames, short forms, role words and typos, so entity-seeded legs are inert until aliases bind; multi-session evidence needs a hop from a seed hit to related stored items, but a graph built by an LLM per session is costly. String and embedding similarity alone mis-merge short names.
items.gap: I54 confirmed and OBS-01 proposes write.vocative_alias_v2 (S68). R14 adds: LLM-free semantic/temporal link table (Hindsight) so multi-evidence recall does not depend on extract_graph calls, context-weighted merge score (name 0.5, co-occurrence 0.3, time 0.2), and the rule that tentative aliases stay 'maybe same'.
items.hypothesis: A link table built at write with no extra LLM call (temporal within 24 h, semantic kNN, entity co-occurrence) plus one-hop expansion from semantic seeds lifts all-gold coverage on the cross-session set, and a context-weighted merge score cuts wrong merges on open-cast data.
items.evidence: 9 questions targeted by vocative/short-form binding (74 detected turns); entity leg inert until the graph arm builds entities; link expansion shares the 43 cross-session questions with M-2

solutions.mechanism: Write-time temporal, semantic and entity-co-occurrence links; one-hop expansion from seeds at read.

items.title: Image captions: misattributed or photo-only evidence
items.problem: The answer is in an image caption but the reader uses a caption from another turn, or the gold fact exists only in the photo. Captions rendered inline in speech make ownership unclear; ingest-time description records are the common engine pattern, not read-time fetch.
items.gap: C7 (caption rule 85.8 vs 86.7, not adopted) confirmed. R14 adds the engine finding that Mem0, Hindsight, MemOS and EverOS describe images at ingest.
items.hypothesis: Rendering each caption on its own typed line with turn id, speaker and date lowers cross-turn mixing (3 of 6); photo-only golds are not fixable here (+2 to +3 questions).
items.evidence: 6 caption-misuse rows (3 cross-turn mixing); 28 caption-only questions; 55 caption-decisive in OBS-05

items.title: Speaker attribution: wrong-speaker answers are rare, but swapped-speaker golds penalise correct attribution
items.problem: Attribution by speaker is the right behaviour, yet in a set of questions the gold turn is spoken by the other person, so a system that ignores the named speaker gains and one that enforces it loses. Restatement can also erase who said it (speaker labels discarded).
items.gap: New: perspective features are scored against labels that sometimes contradict them; no stratum separates the 23 credited swapped-speaker rows.
items.hypothesis: Reporting the swapped-speaker rows as their own stratum explains any perspective-feature loss up to 1.5 points and prevents rejecting a correct attribution feature; owner tags stay tags, not filters.
items.evidence: 1 reader-side wrong-speaker row; 39 speaker-swapped questions of which 23 are credited and not in the errata; 5 speaker candidates still to verify

solutions.name: Speaker-swap stratum in every report
solutions.mechanism: Report the swapped rows separately.

solutions.name: Per-speaker perspective ingestion
solutions.mechanism: Keep speaker as subject/owner on restated facts.

obs.title: Name variants and entity linking
obs.gap: Resolver sees only subject/object of extracted assertions; nickname table is a closed lexicon without a prefix/short-form rule; a bare given name against a full name is only pending_merge; vocatives and query names never use aliases; the reference run extracts nothing so nothing is resolved.
obs.proposal: write.vocative_alias_v2: in the stamping step detect a greeting/vocative token and bind it to a participant by exact match, nickname table, or unique >=3-letter prefix of exactly one participant; set typed addressee, learn the alias (learned.alias marker), tag alias:<token>; optional read.alias_expand for the BM25 leg. Bind nothing when ambiguous.
obs.model_calls: 0 per turn, window, session and read

obs.title: Decontextualise turns into standalone dated statements
obs.status: built-off (window_extract + W2 stack); index view missing
obs.gap: A restated fact is a separate record competing in the pool; the index of the turn itself never improves (ingest/write.py:626 embeds record.content, there is no embed_text); no verdict exists for any write-v2 screen.
obs.proposal: Step 1 write.index_view=context: deterministic embed/BM25 text '{speaker}, {session date}, {topic}: {text}' with the read-side resolved date, content and lineage unchanged. Step 2: the gated restate stage of OBS-03 writes a grounded derived child whose slot goes to the source turn (facts_to_sources).

obs.title: Context carry-over within a session; when to rephrase
obs.gap: No decision about when a turn is incomplete; extraction runs for every window or none; CONTEXT is a read-only coreference aid, not overlap and not an edge; no refers_to link.
obs.proposal: derive/standalone.py (pure): weighted incompleteness score (unresolved pronoun .4, deictic .4, back-reference .4, follow-up question .5, ellipsis .3, missing subject .2; missing time is resolved by rule, not rephrased); rephrase when score >= 0.5; complete turns (named entity + verb + >=6 words) score 0; pure reactions are linked, not rephrased; system/tool/echo skipped. Flagged window -> one window_extract call asking for standalone text and refers_to line numbers; W2-08 grounding drops any rewrite with an entity/number/date not in cited or known lines; stored as a derived child with a context lineage edge.
obs.model_calls: 0 for unflagged windows; 1 per flagged window (about 450 of 1095 six-turn windows on the dataset by the strict rule)

obs.title: Personal profile with attribute history
obs.gap: No default attribute registry (every attribute undeclared); value_history is a projection never rendered to the reader; the card has 5 coarse sections and 24 slots; extractor not wired to ask consent before writing sensitive attributes such as gender.
obs.proposal: offline.person_attributes_v2: declarative registry (attribute -> cardinality, state/event, sensitivity tier, consent purpose) feeding integration_cardinality and the miner; sleep histories stage persists an attribute-timeline derived record per (person, attribute) with dated parents; read.profile_history renders 'attribute: A (until d1) -> B (from d2)' for persons and attributes the query contract targets; user-stated evidence only for active values, assistant-proposed stays tentative; sensitive tiers default-deny without a personalisation:profile grant.
obs.model_calls: no new calls: miner 1 per session and session-close call 2 (1 per session, 272 on the dataset) already specified; timeline build is CPU

obs.title: Layer 3: images and world knowledge
obs.gap: A caption is just words in a turn: no typed image-evidence record, no relevance note, no write-time enrichment layer; external_v2 never plans a lookup for a personal question and takes no caption as input; S23 is inert as configured and egress is undecided.
obs.proposal: write.caption_facts (rule, 0 calls): caption wrapper -> asset_note derived record 'speaker shared a photo: caption' with the turn as parent, tagged asset:caption. Opt-in write.enrich_external: for a caption with a proper-noun/title noun phrase, a privacy-filtered generic lookup stored as a labelled public layer-3 record (family = registrable domain, trust capped, parent = the caption note), rendered only in a separate block, never as a user fact.
obs.model_calls: 0 for caption notes; 1 lookup per enrichable caption, bounded by external_max_calls

obs.title: Inference from memory, not only retrieval
obs.status: partial (harness variants, planner probes built-off, no screen)
obs.gap: (a) Reader: the clauses that commit are not gated by shape; grounded_v2 regressed (81.5 vs 86.7, 5 gained / 17 lost) because a yes/no rule leaked into when/what answers. (b) Retrieval: 28 answers have no gold turn in any leg because the evidence is indirect (an activity implying a preference). True HyDE leg not built.
obs.proposal: read.inference_mode: when the contract says request=inference, append a commit-first clause with a one-line reason that cites a memory line (other shapes keep grounded byte-identical; answer marked inferred in the render; checker drops an answer citing a missing line). Probes: planner v2 restricted to inference reads yields 2 subqueries naming activities or traits that imply each option; rule fallback '{person} {option noun}' from the 'A or B' structure; fused as RRF legs.
obs.model_calls: prompt: 0; probes: 1 planner call per inference-shaped read (about 5% of reads)

obs.title: Session and window summaries
obs.status: built-off (screens queued; S33 fired zero calls)
obs.gap: No window stride/overlap (segmentation: 'no overlap and no gap in NEW lines'); CONTEXT is a read-only coreference aid; topic is not required on every summary; nothing measured.
obs.proposal: write.window_overlap_turns (default 0): windows of size N advance by N-overlap; overlapping turns eligible in both windows, evidence deduped by write_id; add topic (lower-case plural class) to the episode and session-summary schemas and use it as a view tag (view_tag_leg). Decide the overlap only after S31/S33/S61 show the episode leg finds evidence the turn legs miss.
obs.model_calls: windows of 4 stride 3: 1958 on the dataset vs 1095 for 6/6; session level: 272

obs.title: Link new turns to older facts; synonym and paraphrase query expansion
obs.status: partial (all probes built-off, no screen; HyDE leg not built)
obs.gap: No rule paraphrase/synonym probe, no HyDE leg, no backreference detection or refers_to edge; measurements show lexical mismatch is not the failure driver where the vector leg finds the gold.
obs.proposal: read.paraphrase_probes: up to 2 probes per read (planner-v2 subqueries when bound, else rules: statement form + closed verb-synonym swaps), fused as RRF legs at weight 0.5. write.backref_link: rule-detect a backreference phrase, retrieve the best two earlier turns of the same pair by the embedding of the noun phrase after it, write a refers_to lineage edge above a calibrated floor; the antecedent rides with the hit.
obs.model_calls: 0 by rules; 1 per read with the planner; backref: 1 vector query per backreference turn, 0 model calls

obs.title: Plural and pronoun enrichment
obs.gap: A group referent ('the kids') has no field: persons lists named people only; 'we' resolves to speaker plus unknown; unmeasured.
obs.proposal: referents: [{surface, resolves_to, kind, count, source_turns}] on the restate item, required only for gate-flagged pronouns; grounding requires resolves_to and count to occur in cited or CONTEXT lines else the referent is dropped; render '[they = the kids (2)]' as an annotation beside the line, stored text unchanged.

obs.title: Multi-entity and multi-hop questions as map-reduce
obs.status: partial (retired: slot loop, fact chain; built-off, unscreened: agentic query loop, planner v3 persons)
obs.gap: No decomposition into per-entity sub-questions and no combine step: one pooled search for a two-person question is dominated by the better-covered entity; the agentic loop searches again but has no entity quota or combine rule.
obs.proposal: read.decompose_v2: (1) rule detection (>=2 targets that are participants or known entities plus a set operator, comparison, per-entity count or before/after; shared-event verbs without an operator are not decomposed); (2) map: one sub-read per entity with a person filter and an equal token quota, cap 3, parallel, one shared rerank pass; (3) reduce in code: evidence table (entity, value, source line, date) and operators intersection, union, difference, compare, count (distinct merged events), before/after; reader answers from the table; (4) a missing operand reports which entity lacks evidence (obligations hole).
obs.model_calls: 0 extra for detection and map; 1 reader call as today; optional planner v3 persons +1

obs.title: Dates on facts and context
obs.gap: For a non-relative event the only date on a line is the said-date; the happened-date is a read-time annotation on relative phrases and is lost once the line leaves context; event time lives on the extracted fact, not on the turn the reader sees; cross-fact ordering by event time is best effort.
obs.proposal: Fold into OBS-02/03: the restate item carries happened (ISO, precision, basis explicit|relative|inferred|unknown) from the existing anchor ladder; render '[said d1 | happened d2]' for restated lines and the raw line plus [= date] otherwise; read.timeline_block: a compact sorted event list for questions whose contract time view is order or duration (span_line generalised to n events).
